scope: Proposition 5.2 (First-sharing comparison input) of the manuscript “The Weak Inhomogeneous Duffin–Schaeffer Conjecture” (preprints/The-weak-inhomogeneous-Duffin-Schaeffer-conjecture-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 022 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d91ccb7b68c5b0e2), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 25. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For the selected finite blocks, there is a static additional birth test, depending only on the row data and squarefree low numerator moduli and not on the running tables, with arbitrarily small relative first-mass loss against the hard birth means, such that the following statements hold. For any fixed required absolute C, the sum, over first-sharing times and centre pairs, of the broad currencies (5.9) for point pairs at distance at most Cr+ xy is O(1). For exact same-width, same-remaining-mask point pairs in one new cell, sum the currencies (5.7), excluding pairs from the same old child and including all newborn self and diagonal contributions. This sum is ≪ W + Ok0 (W1+c ) (5.10) for a fixed c > 0. Both bounds are uniform in the finite block and in prior table histories obeying the stated operations and core symmetries. The constants in (5.10) may depend on the preceding fixed cutoffs but not on N0.
